notes:
This map combines official population and employment statistics with modeled spatial allocation and commuting flows. It does not use an observed origin-destination commuting table.

RESIDENCE DATA

The population baseline is IBGE's 2022 Census, using total inhabitants in census tracts (setores censitários), including children and retirees. These are irregular statistical areas, not a uniform grid or individual building counts; rural tracts can be substantially larger than urban ones.
OSM and Overture building footprints help identify residential locations. Generic footprint-area and height weights guide the selection of residential anchors, with land-use filtering to avoid unsuitable locations. These are not official per-building dwelling or occupancy records. Where suitable buildings are unavailable, populated census polygons provide fallback locations. Demand points aggregate nearby locations while preserving the allocated census totals.
Resident workers are estimated by applying PNAD Contínua Q2 2026 employed-to-total-population ratios to the 2022 population. Separate ratios are used for Rio de Janeiro, the remainder of the metropolitan area, and small areas outside it. Worker counts are therefore modeled at fine scales, not directly observed by census tract. The full population is not projected to 2026.

WORKPLACE DATA
IBGE CEMPRE 2024 municipal employment figures provide spatial weights for job destinations. RAIS 2023 neighborhood employment shares provide additional detail within Rio de Janeiro municipality only. These are establishment/register-based sources; verified physical workplace coordinates are not available for every worker.
For partially covered municipalities, the population share inside the map approximates the employment share covered. This may misrepresent areas where industrial or commercial activity is concentrated outside residential areas.
Within-area placement uses mapped industrial/commercial activity, residential services and generic activity weights. It does not use official building footprints with measured job capacities. Outside Rio de Janeiro municipality, neighborhood-level job distributions are modeled rather than observed.
The formal component represents 62.2% of modeled workers, based on the complement of PNAD’s metropolitan informality rate of 37.8%. Informal employment is approximated using 75% residential distribution and 25% formal employment geography. This spatial split is an explicit modeling assumption, not an observed distribution.
PNAD, CEMPRE and RAIS cover different statistical populations. They provide employment rates and spatial weights rather than interchangeable counts that can be added together. The RAIS record labeled “Não Identificado,” containing 6,259 employment relationships without geographic coordinates, is excluded from neighborhood spatial allocation. Aggregate “Todos” records are not added to their component categories, avoiding double counting.

RESIDENCE DATA
Resident population comes from IBGE’s 2022 Census, using final census-tract boundaries and attributes. The source counts all inhabitants, including children and retirees. Brazilian census tracts are irregular statistical areas; their sizes vary, particularly between urban and rural locations.
OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps building footprints identify suitable residential locations. Building area and height provide generic weighting assumptions, with land-use filtering to avoid unsuitable locations. These are not official per-building dwelling counts or measured occupancy figures. Populated census polygons provide fallback locations where suitable mapped buildings are unavailable. Nearby locations are aggregated into demand points while preserving allocated census totals.
Resident workers are estimated using IBGE PNAD Contínua Q2 2026 figures from Tables 4093 and 5918. Employed-to-total-population ratios are approximately 49.77% for Rio de Janeiro municipality, 45.97% for the remainder of the metropolitan area, and 47.89% for small covered areas outside the metropolitan region.
These aggregate ratios are applied to the 2022 census population. Fine-scale employed-resident counts are therefore estimates, not direct neighborhood or census-tract measurements. The full population is not projected to 2026. Employment rates using the population aged 14 or older, and unemployment rates using the labor force, are not applied directly to the all-age population.

COMMUTING
A gravity model using road-path travel times balances estimated workers at residential origins against modeled job targets. Individual flows are synthetic. Although official statistics inform the targets, these are not independently measured employed-resident and workplace totals at every modeled area’s resolution.
No observed commuting matrix, inbound/outbound commuting totals or trip-distance survey is used. Total jobs equal modeled resident workers within the map; external commuting across the map boundary is not explicitly modeled.
Employed residents are not necessarily daily commuters. Remote work, part-time schedules, multiple jobs, vacations and weekly commuting frequency are not individually modeled. University students are not automatically counted as employees.
Final allocations use integer counts. Residential worker totals are preserved, while small differences between regional job targets and realized allocations can result from rounding and are recorded in the employment reports.

RELEASE REPRESENTATION
The study-area census population is 11,522,312. The release represents 5,533,862 resident workers in demand_data.json: each point’s residents field equals the sum of its resident commuter groups.
This exported field represents modeled workers, not the complete census population. Non-workers receive no artificial commuting trips. Census totals remain in the source data, reports and map configuration. Unused demand anchors are omitted from the release.

SOURCES AND VINTAGES
- IBGE Census 2022: final census-tract boundaries and population attributes; residents, municipality identification and study-area coverage.
- IBGE PNAD Contínua, Table 4093, Q2 2026: employed population and metropolitan informality rate.
- IBGE PNAD Contínua, Table 5918, Q2 2026: total population denominators for estimating employed-to-total-population ratios.
- IBGE CEMPRE, Table 9509, 2024: employed personnel in establishments by municipality, used as workplace spatial weights.
- RAIS neighborhood employment map, Portal da Geografia Econômica Carioca, 2023: formal employment shares within Rio de Janeiro municipality.
- OpenStreetMap and Overture Maps: building footprints and mapped geographic features used for spatial placement. These are evolving datasets rather than census-year measurements.
